subject: Model pin request + 90-day overlap window — Greenline readiness & comms
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Model pin request + 90-day overlap window — Greenline readiness & comms

Team —

Greenline (Alex Wu) is asking us to pin a specific model variant (rwinf-v2-lowlat-16q) for their high-throughput inference pipeline and to guarantee a 90-day overlap window when we phase the older endpoint down. They cite strict validation and regulatory QA that requires parallel runs.

Key asks from Greenline:
- Pin rwinf-v2-lowlat-16q for the account and ensure traffic routing stays stable for 90 days after we announce deprecation of the legacy endpoint.
- A clear comms schedule and a rollback hatch if model-quality drift is observed during overlap.

What I need from each function:
- Marissa (Product): confirm whether pinning this variant is okay from compatibility and rollout/variant policy perspective. Are there any runtime constraints (memory, batch limits) we should call out to the customer?
- Ben (Sales/CS): confirm mutual action plan (MAP) cadence and whether Greenline has test harnesses we should run during overlap. Also, does this trigger any contract/discount ask?
- Neha (Reliability/Ops): what are the operational costs and capacity implications for reserving the variant for a single account for 90 days? Any autoscale or isolation recommendations?
- Priya (Legal/Privacy): will we need an amendment for a pinned variant or SLA deviation documented?

Attachments: pin request form (greenline_pin_request_form.pdf) and a proposed timeline (greenline_migration_timeline.xlsx) + a first-draft customer comms note.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- 2026-10-09: internal sign-off (product + ops + legal)
- 2026-10-16: notify Greenline of schedule and provide comms draft
- 2026-10-23: start 90-day overlap window (customer begins parallel validation)
- 2026-01-21: finish overlap, legacy endpoint retired for Greenline

Please reply with clear owners and any blocking concerns by EOD 2026-10-06. If we cannot meet 10/09 internal sign-off, propose the earliest feasible date and explain blockers.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Strategy — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-02T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Model pin request + 90-day overlap window — Greenline readiness & comms

Thanks Dylan — quick read:

1) Product constraints: we can pin rwinf-v2-lowlat-16q for a single tenant but there are caveats:
   - Quantized 16-bit variant has a smaller KV cache headroom; for long sequences concurrent sessions > 8 may see memory pressure. We should state "recommended concurrent sessions <= 8" in the comms.
   - Some of the new attention kernels are still behind the progressive rollout flag; we'll need to opt the pinned variant into the stable kernel set for the overlap window. Ops will need to coordinate kernel pinning.

2) Rollout/compat policy: this is an exception to our default model consolidation policy. I can sign off on a 90-day overlap if we document the exception reason and an owner for metric monitoring (latency P95, token rejection rate, deterministic output checks).

Action items I own:
- Draft an exception memo for the model consolidation council by 2026-10-07.
- Add the recommended restrictions (concurrent sessions, sequence length) to the comms draft.

Marissa
Product — Redwood Inference

Looping Alex here so Greenline has visibility into our internal cadence. Alex — thanks for raising this. Short answers from my side:

- MAP and validation: Greenline has committed to running the parallel validation but asked for a list of automated checks we will run on our side (latency, tokenization parity, sample-based semantic drift checks). If Ops can provide a daily health summary during the overlap that would satisfy their audit.
- Commercial: a pin often triggers an operational credit ask. We should be prepared for a one-time credit or a short-term uplift, not a long-term discount. I will flag this to RevOps but need a rough cost delta from Neha to put numbers on the table.

Proposed customer-facing plan (week-by-week high level):
- Week 0 (announce): shared comms + recommended test harness + sign MOA (mutual action plan).
- Week 1–12 (overlap): daily health pings, weekly syncs, a mid-overlap checkpoint at week 6, and a final sign-off at week 12.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from Greenline: 

- We will run the parallel validation on our staging environment and can provide test harness logs daily. We do require a daily health summary from Redwood (latency P95, error rate, sample semantic checks).
- On the credit: we expect the pin to be treated operationally as an SLA deviation; an operational credit for the 90-day reserved capacity is reasonable. Please send a draft estimate so procurement can review.
- Rollback hatch: if we see >2% semantic drift versus our production baseline across 48 hours, we will request a pause. We need confirmation Redwood can route us back to the legacy endpoint for at least 48 hours without re-training or client-side changes.

Next steps per Greenline:
1) Provide the daily health summary format and an example (ops)
2) Share estimated cost delta for pin (Neha)
3) Share updated comms + MOA (Ben/Marissa)
4) Legal amendment draft if needed (Priya)

Alex Wu
Head of ML Platform — Greenline Analytics
